summary.title: Self-assembling materials mimicking dynamic bio-interfaces in cellular activities
summary.executive_summary: This feature article reviews the development of bioinspired supramolecular materials designed to mimic dynamic bio-interfaces critical for cellular activities. The authors highlight three primary areas of innovation: the construction of artificial extracellular matrices (ECMs) using self-assembling peptide hydrogels to enhance neuronal migration in injured brains; the creation of peptide fibres capable of efficient incorporation and sustained release of growth factors like VEGF for tissue regeneration; and the engineering of stimuli-responsive systems, including redox-controlled cargo release and highly stable phospholipid nanosheets for extended blood circulation. Additionally, the article describes a molecular machine approach to induce endocytosis-like fission in liposomes for the efficient encapsulation and in vivo delivery of viruses. By combining supramolecular chemistry with nanotechnology, these materials aim to reconstruct the dynamic nature of natural bio-interfaces, offering new strategies for regenerative medicine and advanced drug delivery systems. The review underscores the potential of bottom-up methodologies to manipulate biological interfaces, moving from static scaffolds to dynamic, functional systems that actively participate in cellular processes such as adhesion, signal transduction, and substance transportation.

judge_context:
Executive Summary
This feature article reviews the development of bioinspired supramolecular materials designed to mimic dynamic bio-interfaces critical for cellular activities. The authors highlight three primary areas of innovation: the construction of artificial extracellular matrices (ECMs) using self-assembling peptide hydrogels to enhance neuronal migration in injured brains; the creation of peptide fibres capable of efficient incorporation and sustained release of growth factors like VEGF for tissue regeneration; and the engineering of stimuli-responsive systems, including redox-controlled cargo release and highly stable phospholipid nanosheets for extended blood circulation. Additionally, the article describes a molecular machine approach to induce endocytosis-like fission in liposomes for the efficient encapsulation and in vivo delivery of viruses. By combining supramolecular chemistry with nanotechnology, these materials aim to reconstruct the dynamic nature of natural bio-interfaces, offering new strategies for regenerative medicine and advanced drug delivery systems. The review underscores the potential of bottom-up methodologies to manipulate biological interfaces, moving from static scaffolds to dynamic, functional systems that actively participate in cellular processes such as adhesion, signal transduction, and substance transportation.

Research Context
Cellular functions rely on dynamic actions at bio-interfaces. Extracellular matrices regulate migration and differentiation. Phospholipid bilayers enable substance transportation. Stimuli-responsive transformation is a notable characteristic. Recent progress enables creation of dynamic materials. Artificial ECMs and membrane-deforming materials are introduced.

Research Question And Hypothesis
Can self-assembling peptides mimic ECM to enhance migration? Does N-cadherin conjugation improve neuroblast migration? Can peptide fibres incorporate and release full-length proteins? Do JigSAP motifs enable efficient protein binding? Can redox-active peptides control cargo release kinetics? Can peptide-stabilized nanosheets enable extended circulation? Can molecular machines induce endocytosis-like fission?

Methodological Details
Peptide fibres are recognized as versatile supramolecular scaffolds. RADA16 peptides form nanofibres via hydrogen bonding. A8G mutants form bundled nanofibres and robust hydrogels. A16G mutants form curved fibres seen on TEM. Neuroblasts are derived from endogenous neural stem cells. JigSAP possesses jigsaw-shaped hydrophobic surfaces. JigSAP incorporates VEGF for regenerative therapeutic effects. Redox-active peptides contain methionine residues. Met is oxidised by reactive oxygen species such as H2O2. Cholic acid derivatives localize at the edge of membranes. DPPC/Chol-MBP nanosheets are formed with a 5/1 ratio. AzoMEx contains a diazocine core for mechanical motion. AzoMEx undergoes opening-closing motion by photoisomerization. M13 phages are used to test encapsulation efficiency.

Procedures And Architectures
Peptide amphiphiles construct nanofibres by forming cylindrical micelles. A16G hydrogel shows lower stiffness than RADA16. A16G-Ncad is a mixture of A16G and A16G-Ncad. JigSAP sequence is Ac-RIDARMRADIR-NH2. JigSAP forms nanofibres with an average width of 3.2 nm. JigSAP hydrogel exhibits a remarkably high rigidity. EGFP-JigSAP is incorporated at 93 mol%. JigSAP-IMI and JigSAP-MII form hydrogels under physiological conditions. JigSAP-IMI-Ox remains dispersed in solution. 30% H2O2 aq. is added to induce gel-sol transition. Chol-MBP binds to two Cu 2+ ions. Nanosheets are diluted to 0.2 wt% for stability testing. Cu 2+ ions are added at 2.0 equivalents. Mice are administered via the tail vein. AzoMEx is embedded in DOPC-based giant unilamellar vesicles. M13 phages are 1-µm long anionic viruses. Encapsulated phages are coated with a block polymer.

Key Results
Migration rate was significantly higher with A16G-Ncad. Dcx+ neuroblasts are abundantly observed in A16G-Ncad mixtures. Neuroblasts are seen sparsely in A16G alone. EGFP-JigSAP incorporation efficiency is 93 mol%. Non-tagged EGFP incorporation is only 3 mol%. EGFP-5V shows 66 mol% incorporation efficiency. EGFP-RADA16 shows 55 mol% incorporation efficiency. 21 mol% of EGFP-JigSAP is released after 24 hours. 39 mol% is released after 168 hours. EGFP-5V release stagnates after 48 hours. Only 5 mol% of EGFP-5V is released after 168 hours. JigSAP hydrogel rigidity is 1.1 x 10 4 Pa. Double-positive cells increase with VEGF-JigSAP injection. Nanosheets are maintained upon dilution with Cu 2+. Vesicles were aggregated and clogged. Nanosheets were homogeneously dispersed in blood vessels. Spleen infectivity was [25.6 ± 13.2] × 10 9 virions/mg. Liver infectivity was [18.3 ± 3.2] × 10 9 virions/mg. Brain infectivity was [0.2 ± 0.1] × 10 9 virions/mg.

Interpretation And Theoretical Implications
Fibrous selfassembly mimics structure and dynamic function. Point mutations control dynamic properties. Redox modification controls kinetics. Stabilized bicelles are functional for extended circulation. Molecular machines trigger outside-in membrane deformation. Outside-in deformation allows efficient encapsulation. Encapsulated viruses can be delivered to multiple organs. Supramolecular approaches present powerful ways for regenerative medicines.

Contradictions And Limitations
Secreted protein incorporation and release are generally incompatible. Bicelles are essentially unstable and tend to undergo phase transitions. AzoMEx technology is still in its infancy. Materials science to reconstruct biomimetic interfaces is expected to make significant progress.

Claims
Self-assembling peptide hydrogels can mimic ECM to enhance neuronal migration in injured brains. Migration rate was significantly higher with A16G-Ncad. Dcx+ neuroblasts are abundantly observed in A16G-Ncad mixtures. Neuroblasts are seen sparsely in A16G alone. Provides a novel strategy for neuro-regenerative therapy.
JigSAP peptide fibres enable efficient incorporation and sustained release of full-length proteins. EGFP-JigSAP is incorporated at 93 mol%. 21 mol% is released after 24 hours. Non-tagged EGFP incorporation is only 3 mol%. EGFP-5V release stagnates after 48 hours. Demonstrates wide applicability to controlled sustained release.
Redox-responsive peptides allow kinetics-controlled cargo release. JigSAP-IMI-Ox remains dispersed in solution. 30% H2O2 aq. induces gel-sol transition. JigSAP-IMI forms hydrogels under physiological conditions. Useful for drug and cargo release.
Peptide-stabilized phospholipid nanosheets enable extended blood circulation. Nanosheets were homogeneously dispersed in blood vessels. Spleen infectivity was [25.6 ± 13.2] × 10 9 virions/mg. Vesicles were aggregated and clogged. Suitable carrier to the whole body by blood administration.
Molecular machines induce endocytosis-like fission for virus delivery. AzoMEx undergoes opening-closing motion by photoisomerization. M13 phages are efficiently incorporated. Endocytosis-like transport remains critically unexplored. Could be applied to an in vivo phage display method.

Robustness And Ablation Notes
Ablation of N-cadherin reduces neuroblast migration. Ablation of JigSAP tag reduces protein incorporation. Ablation of Cu 2+ causes nanosheet instability.

Key Figures Tables
Figure 1 illustrates dynamic functions of bio-interfaces. Figure 2a shows conformational flexibility of peptide fibres. Figure 3a shows migration rate of neuroblasts. Figure 4h shows incorporation efficiency of EGFP. Figure 6f shows vesicle aggregation. Figure 7o-t shows plaque assays of organs.

Three Takeaways
1. Self-assembling peptides mimic ECM to enhance neuronal migration. 2. JigSAP enables efficient incorporation and sustained release of proteins. 3. Molecular machines enable endocytosis-like fission for virus delivery.
